11c_1_components_linear_history.png: The normalised Lovelock tensors $E_{(1)}$ (Einstein), $E_{(2)}$ and $E_{(3)}$ of the corrected metric on the histories $a_4 = A H x_4$, $b_4 = b_4(0) e^{(4/3) A H x_4}$, in units of $H^2$, $H^4$ and $H^6$: the time component (solid), the space component (dashed) and the common component of the hidden direction and the extra times (dotted). Top: against the slope $A$ at the moment where $k = e^{2 a_4}/b_4 = 1$; every curve is symmetric about $A = 0$, the reversal of the time. Bottom: along the history of the record, $A = 1$, against the time $H x_4$, where $k = e^{2 H x_4/3}$ grows; for $k = 1$ the curves are $A^2/3 + 6k$, $6k - 13A^2/9$ and $3k - 11A^2/3$.
11c_2_lovelock_scalars.png: The Lovelock scalars $L_{(1)} = 2R$, $L_{(2)}$ and $L_{(3)}$ of the corrected metric along the history of the record, $a_4 = H x_4$, $b_4 = e^{(4/3) H x_4}$, in units of $H^2$, $H^4$ and $H^6$, against the time $H x_4$; on this history each is a polynomial in $k = e^{2 H x_4/3}$: $L_{(1)} = 112/9 - 24k$ vanishes at $k = 14/27$, $L_{(2)}$ at one positive $k$, and $L_{(3)}$, a quadratic in $k$ with positive coefficients, never; the black dots mark the zeros. At $x_4 = 0$ the three values are $-104/9$, $-21728/27$ and $93184/9$.
11c_3_test_history.png: The illustrative test history $a_4 = H x_4 + \frac{1}{2} \ln\cosh H x_4$, $b_4 = e^{(4/3) a_4}$, not a solution of any field equation, against the time $H x_4$. Left: the scale factor $e^{a_4}$ of ordinary space (solid) grows and the scale factor $e^{-a_4} b_4^{1/2} = e^{-a_4/3}$ of the hidden direction and the extra times (dashed) shrinks at all times, both on a logarithmic axis, where exponential change is a straight line whose slope steepens around $x_4 = 0$. Right: $a_4^{\prime}/H$ rises from 1/2 to 3/2 with $u = 4a_4^{\prime}/3$, and $a_4^{\prime\prime}/H^2$ and $v = 4a_4^{\prime\prime}/3$ are bumps at $x_4 = 0$.
11c_4_components_test_history.png: The three independent components of $E_{(1)}$, $E_{(2)}$ and $E_{(3)}$ along the illustrative test history, in units of $H^2$, $H^4$, $H^6$, against the time $H x_4$: the time component $E^{x_4}_{\ x_4}$ (solid), the space component $E^{x_1}_{\ x_1}$ (dashed) and the common component $E^{x_0}_{\ x_0} = E^{x_5}_{\ x_5}$ of the hidden direction and the extra times (dotted). Top: the components, which grow with $k$. Bottom: the part that the second derivatives $a_4^{\prime\prime}$ and $v = 4a_4^{\prime\prime}/3$, a bump around $x_4 = 0$, contribute; it enters the space and block components linearly and is exactly 0 for the time component, which depends on $a_4^{\prime}$, $u$ and $k$ only.
11c_5_conservation_identity.png: Identity (I), the conservation identity along the time, checked numerically along the illustrative test history for $k = 1, 2, 3$: the finite-difference derivative of the time component $E^{x_4}_{\ x_4}$ (dotted black) lies on the right side $3 a_4^{\prime} (E^{x_1}_{\ x_1} - E^{x_4}_{\ x_4}) + 4 h_4 (E^{x_0}_{\ x_0} - E^{x_4}_{\ x_4})$ with $h_4 = u/2 - a_4^{\prime}$ (thick blue), in units of $H^{2k+1}$, against the time $H x_4$; the largest relative deviation is about $6.8 \times 10^{-5}$, the size of the finite-difference error.
